Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

for preposition

a length of time

also for two days, for an hour, for a week, all night, all day, for the next two days, for ten days, for the last three months, for the following day

classical

Cic. Fam. 14.2.3: diēs noctēsque versāris
Cic. Tusc. 2.40: inediam bīduum aut trīduum ferunt
Traupman 317

cāsus accūsātīvus

construction: the length of time in the accusative, with no preposition

for (how long)

Only with words of time (hōram, diem, bīduum, annum). A distance or a thing is not a length of time: “he slept the whole journey” is per tōtum iter dormīvit, not tōtum iter. Age is said the same way: decem annōs nātus.

Other words

  • per + acc. — for, all through (a time)

    preposition with the accusative · also used · classical · Liv. 21.33.11: per trīduum exercitum aluit; Liv. 22.2.7: per quadrīduum jam et trēs noctēs

    Stresses that it lasted the whole time; see also during.

  • in + acc. — for (a time ahead: what is meant to last)

    preposition with the accusative · also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 191: in hoc bīduum, Thāis, valē; Traupman 317

    “For tomorrow”, in crāstinum; “for ever”, in perpetuum.

Examples

  • nam mihi ante oculōs diēs noctēsque versāris

    for you are before my eyes day and nightCic. Fam. 14.2.3

  • aniculae saepe inediam bīduum aut trīduum ferunt

    little old women often go without food for two or three daysCic. Tusc. 2.40

  • mustum sī volēs tōtum annum habēre, in amphoram mustum inditō et corticem oppicātō, dēmittitō in piscīnam. post diēs XXX eximitō. tōtum annum mustum erit

    if you want grape juice all year, put the juice in a jar, pitch the cork and sink it in the pond; take it out after thirty days; there will be grape juice all yearCato Agr. 120

  • captō cibō ac pecoribus per trīduum exercitum aluit

    with the food and the flocks he had captured he fed the army for three daysLiv. 21.33.11

  • In hoc bīduum, Thāis, valē. — Mī Phaedria, et tū; numquid vīs aliud?

    Goodbye for these two days, Thais. — And you, my Phaedria; is there anything else?Ter. Eun. 190–191

  • cētera intēctī tōtōs diēs jūxtā focum atque ignem agunt

    otherwise unclothed, they spend whole days by the hearth and the fireTac. Germ. 17.1

  • decem diēs

    for ten daysTraupman 317

  • Eam ad cēnam vocāvit in posterum diem.

    He invited her to dinner for the following day.Traupman 317

  • in ternōs novissimōs mēnsēs

    for the last three monthsTraupman 317

See also long, during, since, until.
